summary: When Nora mentions what she saw on someone's story, she says it was their story and roughly when — not what she now knows about them.
details: A story is gone in a day. What Nora SAYS about it is not: her side of a conversation is kept as things she has learned about people, permanently. So «he was at the gym» quietly turns something she glimpsed once into something she knows, and a week later nothing can tell the two apart. «His story this morning» goes stale honestly, because it says where it came from and when.
The instruction to phrase it that way now rides along with the story itself, so it arrives exactly when she is deciding how to say it — and costs nothing on every other thing she does.
limitations: It is a phrasing she is told to use, not something enforced afterwards. It makes the honest wording the obvious one; it cannot make a model that ignores it say something else.
It only covers what she read from a story. Anything she works out by putting a story next to something else she knows is not touched by this.
